belongs_to: Puzzle Time - Navakankari: the game board with the two sets of pawns and the Gameplay rules (book p.135)
description: Square game board on a teal woven-cloth background with a dark ornamental floral border band. Inside, THREE nested squares (outer, middle, inner; side lengths roughly 3 : 2 : 1) drawn with thin brown-red lines and sharing the same centre. Each square has 8 round orange points: its 4 corners and the 4 midpoints of its sides, so 24 points in all; the points are joined along the sides of each square. Four straight cross lines join the side-midpoints of the three squares: one each from the top, bottom, left and right midpoints of the outer square through the middle square's midpoint to the inner square's midpoint (so each side midpoint is on a line of 3 points). At the exact centre, inside the inner square, is a round sun-face medallion (not a playing point); short line stubs from the four innermost midpoints lead towards it. No pawn is on the board. To the left of the board is a loose group of 9 dark-brown pawns; to the right is a loose group of 9 yellow pawns (each pawn a small bell/cone with a round knob).
unclear: Whether the cross lines join the medallion at the centre or stop short of it is not clear; the medallion is not a playing point.
